SRC-325:R001.text: MISSION Eliminate the recurring class of operational deadlocks in which a recoverable malformed checkpoint prevents SAIPEN from admitting or continuing legitimate user-requested engineering work. The triggering incident was observed during a Freebuff Desktop startup repair. The agent received a genuine operator request to fix a broken application launcher, but SAIPEN reconciliation refused further execution because the project's canonical STATE/BOARD/LOG were not mutually consistent. The agent then performed technical repairs through workspace tools outside the canonical SAIPEN work lifecycle. This is a protocol availability and accountability failure. The intended result: - Mechanically recoverable protocol drift is repaired without operator intervention. - Truly ambiguous authority remains protected. - A malformed advisory next_action does not automatically become a permanent execution blockade. - Urgent, already-authorized engineering work has a safe interruption and resumption path. - Work performed during a degraded session is subsequently reconciled as evidence, without falsifying its provenance. - Repeated failures do not create infinite recovery loops. Do not introduce an unrestricted emergency bypass. Do not grant authority from agent-generated prose. Do not sacrifice journal integrity for availability.

SRC-325:R002.text: FIELD INCIDENT Consumer project: _FREEBUFF_SAI Reported operator objective: Repair Freebuff Desktop startup, window activation and watcher behavior. Reported initial protocol state: BOARD: T-69 has checkbox [x] but remains in ## DOING. STATE: last_event: 991 LOG: physical tail: E-994 STATE: next_action contains non-conforming descriptive prose. Reported continuation refusal: RECONCILE_REAUTH_REQUIRED Reason: legacy next_action cannot be projected because phase DONE is not ticket-bearing or task is not a Work ticket. Canonical suggested command: saipen recover resolve-next-action <SRC-###> The session reported that the user had already supplied a new urgent practical objective. The protocol nevertheless remained blocked on repairing the old checkpoint projection. Reported consequence: the agent repaired application files through workspace tools without successfully restoring the SAIPEN lifecycle first. Treat all consumer-side implementation and timing claims as field evidence until independently verified. The contemporary consumer repository was not supplied for this protocol investigation.

SRC-325:R003.text: VERIFIED CURRENT ENGINE BEHAVIOR SOURCE: tools/saipen_engine/reconcile.py Existing functions: _checkbox_drifts(), _apply_checkbox_repairs(), _state_marker_repairs(), _state_next_action_repairs(), reconcile_protocol_state() Current behavior already supports mechanical normalization of BOARD checkbox presentation against its canonical section; repair of STATE.last_event from the verified LOG tail; journaled compare-and-swap reconciliation transactions; combined repair planning; preservation of original checkpoint evidence. Do not implement duplicate mechanisms for these capabilities. CONFIRMED RECOVERY GAP: _state_next_action_repairs() refuses an invalid next_action when the persisted phase is not ticket-bearing or the task is not a valid active Work identifier. For phase DONE, task none, invalid legacy prose, the function requests an authenticated operator decision instead of first determining whether the action is merely an obsolete routing projection with a mechanically provable replacement. The current tests intentionally preserve this refusal. RELEVANT TESTS: tools/test_next_action_deadlock.py, tools/test_recovery_reachability.py, tools/test_reconcile_legacy_output_field.py, tools/test_reconcile_history_ledger_blocked.py, tools/test_reconcile_valve.py RELEVANT ROUTING: tools/saipen_engine/router.py::route_next, tools/saipen.py::_continue, tools/saipen_engine/entry.py::start_work RELEVANT VALIDATION: tools/saipen_engine/fast_check.py::validate_texts, tools/saipen_engine/state.py::state_contract_errors, tools/saipen_engine/state.py::patch_state, tools/saipen_engine/phases.py::phase_next_action_error

SRC-325:R004.text: P0 — REPRODUCE THE EXACT COMPOUND FAILURE Construct a disposable Freebuff-shaped fixture: valid project lineage; valid canonical LOG history; STATE.last_event = 991; LOG tail = 994; phase DONE; task none; invalid descriptive next_action; T-69 checkbox [x] inside ## DOING; no independent evidence that T-69 completed; a new legitimate operator-authored urgent request pending. Run the actual saipen continue --json and saipen recover --json. Capture the entire proposed repair set, refusal classification, first blocking condition, canonical suggested action, written bytes, pending user-request preservation, state before and after. Expected pre-fix observation: the next_action operator gate can prevent otherwise safe metadata reconciliation and continuation. Prove or disprove that interaction on the current revision. Do not infer it solely from the field report.

SRC-325:R005.text: P0 — SAFE RECOVERY OF TERMINAL NEXT_ACTION Extend the existing canonical next_action reconciliation rather than creating another router. For an invalid next_action in a non-ticket-bearing phase: N01. Verify the actual phase from canonical lifecycle evidence. N02. Verify the task binding. N03. Verify the complete current journal and its authority. N04. Verify the authoritative current BOARD status. N05. Inspect queued operator requests. N06. Inspect pending Sources. N07. Inspect the canonical audit inbox. N08. Inspect any active execution seat or pending operation. N09. Inspect current authorization and capability. N10. Determine whether the malformed next_action is an obsolete advisory projection or contains genuinely unresolved operator intent. N11. Preserve its original bytes as forensic evidence. N12. Derive the correct next executable operation from the shared router whenever it is uniquely provable. N13. Apply the result through the existing canonical, journaled reconciliation transaction. N14. Revalidate the complete checkpoint after repair. N15. Resume routing immediately when eligible. N16. Do not create an artificial action merely to make the grammar valid. N17. Do not create a recursive saipen continue loop. N18. If all executable work is exhausted, produce the correct terminal or quiescent outcome. N19. If the legacy prose contains potentially unconsumed user intent, preserve it and refuse to discard that intent without independent proof. N20. If the action is genuinely ambiguous, retain the exact operator gate. In particular, a terminal DONE state does not automatically make the advisory next_action authoritative. However, DONE also does not mean that an old descriptive string must permanently block independent new user work.

Where independent safe repairs can be committed without changing the meaning of the unresolved gate, use canonical journaled partial settlement with explicit dependency proof. R08. Where the repairs are inseparable, retain the complete pending plan rather than making repeated identical attempts. R09. Do not return a generic recovery refusal that hides already diagnosed problems. R10. Preserve the exact original bytes and repair intent. R11. Prevent one non-authoritative advisory field from globally blocking unrelated verified work. R12. Never claim CLEAN while a genuine unresolved field remains. R13. Ensure repeated continue calls do not generate identical recovery incidents or consume execution budgets needlessly. R14. Verify a successful repair causes canonical rerouting. R15. Avoid adding another fallback recovery implementation.

Instead verify its behavior under compound checkpoint drift. Required: L01. Validate complete journal continuity. L02. Validate operation-backed history. L03. SRC-325:R009.text: P1 — SAFE URGENT OPERATOR INTERRUPTION Investigate a narrowly scoped, authenticated urgent-work lane. Do not implement an unrestricted bypass command. Desired behavior: U01. Authenticate the actual new operator request. U02. Preserve its original bytes and source identity. U03. Record the request durably through an existing safe intake mechanism where possible. U04. Classify the existing checkpoint failure. U05. Attempt proven-safe recovery first. U06. If the old Work cannot be resumed, preserve its exact blocked state and execution ownership. U07. Determine whether independent local diagnostic or engineering work can proceed with already valid authority and negotiated host capabilities. U08. Do not steal a live execution seat. U09. Do not mutate canonical STATE/BOARD/LOG through arbitrary filesystem tools. U10. Do not treat emergency urgency as approval for publication, destructive actions or unrelated scope expansion. U11. Support read-only diagnosis even when a write path is blocked, where existing read capability permits it. U12. If authorized independent work can proceed safely in an isolated workspace, preserve that ownership and execution identity. U13. Once canonical repair is available, reconcile the observed implementation delta through ordinary Source/Work admission and verification. U14. Do not backdate or forge missing lifecycle history. U15. Preserve clear distinctions between work done before admission, work admitted later, and work verified afterward. U16. Keep operator involvement limited to genuinely missing authority or ambiguous product intent. U17. Return a precise blocker if no safe isolated or authorized execution path exists. U18. Ensure a blocked old request cannot silently erase a fresh authenticated user objective. This lane is for safe interruption and recovery, not for turning protocol corruption into unlimited source-write rights.

SRC-325:R010.text: P1 — RECONCILE WORK PERFORMED OUTSIDE THE LEDGER Create or reuse a safe reconciliation mechanism that: E01. Detects the actual current repository delta. E02. Identifies the modified paths. E03. Compares the work against the genuine operator objective. E04. Preserves original timestamps and available source provenance. E05. Does not fabricate prior Source, LOG or Work events. E06. Does not claim the external work was executed through SAIPEN. E07. Allows subsequent legitimate admission or association through existing Source/Work mechanics. E08. Verifies the actual implementation. E09. Records new verification honestly at its real time. E10. Avoids implementing the same changes again. E11. Keeps publication authority separate. E12. Clearly reports whether pre-admission work was accepted, quarantined, blocked or remains unverified. E13. Preserves exact changed-file identity and test evidence. E14. Never classifies an unverified implementation as DONE solely because the agent reported success.

SRC-325:R012.text: P1 — DIAGNOSTIC CLASSIFICATION Replace vague compound refusal text with a concise structured diagnosis of the complete incident. Proposed classifications: STALE_STATE_MARKER, BOARD_PRESENTATION_DRIFT, LEGACY_NEXT_ACTION, NEXT_ACTION_CANONICALLY_PROJECTABLE, NEXT_ACTION_SEMANTICALLY_AMBIGUOUS, UNTRUSTED_LIFECYCLE_EVENT, GENUINE_OPERATOR_GATE, SAFE_RECOVERY_AVAILABLE, PARTIAL_SAFE_RECOVERY_AVAILABLE, RECOVERY_REQUIRES_AUTHORITY, INDEPENDENT_WORK_ADMISSIBLE, NO_SAFE_EXECUTION_LANE. Use existing protocol result types wherever possible. Do not create another incompatible status framework. Every refusal must state: actual blocking field; exact project and scope; evidence source; whether the problem is mechanical or semantic; whether a safe repair exists; whether a new user request is preserved; whether independent work can continue; the precise next executable action. Do not emit a placeholder decision command as though it were ready to execute. Do not create an operator gate when canonical evidence already proves the necessary outcome.

SRC-325:R013.text: REQUIRED REGRESSION MATRIX AC-01: STATE.last_event lags a complete valid LOG by three events -> canonical repair without new operator approval. AC-02: the same gap contains unauthorized lifecycle events -> no blind fast-forward. AC-03: T-69 is [x] in DOING with no completion proof -> presentation normalized; ticket remains DOING. AC-04: a ticket completion is independently proven -> existing canonical lifecycle rules govern placement. AC-05: DONE/task none carries stale descriptive next_action with no unconsumed intent or independent gate -> safe canonical projection and continuation or quiescent idle. AC-06: DONE/task none carries descriptive next_action that may encode unconsumed user intent -> no silent deletion of intent. AC-07: malformed next_action plus independently repairable LOG drift -> complete diagnosis; safe repair proceeds when independent. AC-08: malformed next_action plus an actual operator-controlled gate -> gate preserved. AC-09: malformed next_action plus a fresh authenticated urgent request -> new request preserved; no accidental loss. AC-10: a read-only host encounters protocol drift -> diagnostic plan only; no false repair claim. AC-11: a canonical operation attempts to persist invalid next_action -> refused before commit. AC-12: a foreign process directly edits STATE -> modification is not credited as a canonical engine event. AC-13: a crash happens before recovery commit -> original checkpoint remains recoverable. AC-14: a crash happens after commit but before response delivery -> idempotent recovery. AC-15: two concurrent writers race recovery -> CAS conflict; no stale mutation. AC-16: repeated unchanged recover calls encounter one genuine gate -> no infinite retry loop. AC-17: a real urgent engineering request is independently authorized, but an unrelated old Work remains blocked -> independent safe work can proceed where the existing capability and authority permit. AC-18: the urgent request requires new authority not present -> correct refusal, no bypass. AC-19: work was performed outside the canonical lifecycle -> real delta and provenance preserved without fabricated history. AC-20: external implementation is incomplete or unverified -> no false DONE. AC-21: external implementation is correct and subsequently admitted -> no redundant reimplementation; current verification recorded. AC-22: an unrelated publication gate remains closed -> no unauthorized push or release. AC-23: another harness resumes after recovery -> identical canonical state and work identity. AC-24: reconcile is repeated after successful settlement -> CLEAN and zero additional writes. AC-25: the installed runtime differs from the development source -> explicit deployment mismatch, not a fabricated live PASS.
